target_customer: Clinical trial sites and doctors offices that enroll patients in pharma trials
problem: Finding eligible patients for clinical trials is manual; HealthKey prescreens existing patient records against eligibility criteria.
business_model: Success fee per qualified patient identified, no upfront cost
product_category: AI patient identification for clinical trials

founders.name: Josh Sabol
founders.background_notes: Education not listed on YC page.

competitors.name: Inato
competitors.what: Clinical trial site network adding AI patient prescreening

technical_complexity.rationale: EHR integrations (Epic, athenahealth, NextGen) and parsing faxed PDFs against protocol criteria.

defensibility.rationale: EHR integrations help, but several AI prescreening startups emerged in 2025.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Peers added AI prescreening in 2025; no acquisition of HealthKey found.

market_need_then: Pharma pays sites per enrolled patient and prescreening is manual (company claim on YC page). A urology practice reportedly found hundreds of eligible patients, self-reported.

brand_strength.rationale: A London company also called HealthKey raised a seed in 2024 per UK Tech News, so the name is confusable; no brand coverage found.

outcome_analysis: HealthKey is an early Austin company from the Winter 2025 batch led by a single named founder with a product background at AWS and Plate IQ. Its pay per patient model lowers adoption risk. No exit, shutdown or disclosed funding was found, and the site claims dozens of sites using it without verification. Competition in AI trial prescreening grew quickly during 2025.
notes: Funding unverified: aggregators say about $500K pre-seed in 2025-03 including Y Combinator; one funding result concerned a different London HealthKey. No second source, so no round recorded. YC page lists only Josh Sabol.
